name: Dense node-context map in Taffy (no std feature)

atomicDiscipline.rule: Run exactly the printed hypothesis. If the attempted change fails, degrades, or suggests a different fix, revert to the checkpoint and finish this experiment as failure. Start a new experiment for the next idea.

hypothesisMarkdown: Taffy with its std feature stores node contexts in a SparseSecondaryMap keyed with std's SipHash RandomState. gpux reads and writes a context for every measured text leaf each frame (clear, set_measure_keeping_clean), so SipHash showed as 25-46 samples of the dashboard-clock main thread. Without the std feature Taffy uses the dense Vec-indexed SecondaryMap.
measurementPlanMarkdown: Drop taffy's std feature (keep alloc), fix the three debug helpers whose ? needs StdError, run the gpux lib tests, then alternate the old and new benchmark binaries three times on dashboard-clock, text-relabel, hover-grid and scroll-div-cards with fast mode on.
reportMarkdown: Allocations and footprint are unchanged. The gpux lib tests pass (1038), clippy and fmt are clean. Taffy's no_std float polyfills (round, floor, ceil) are copies of num-traits and gave identical layouts in the oracle tests.
decisionMarkdown: Keep: a one-line dependency feature change with a consistent 2-11% draw gain and no other cost.
